cards.q: Which plate boundary forms where two plates move away from each other?
cards.why: Divergent boundaries separate plates. Magma rises to fill the gap and forms new oceanic crust at mid-ocean ridges.
cards.trap: Confusing divergent with subduction; subduction is a convergent process where a plate sinks.

cards.q: What happens when an oceanic plate meets a continental plate at a convergent boundary?
choices: The oceanic plate sinks beneath the continental plate
The continental plate sinks beneath the oceanic plate
Both plates slide past each other
cards.answer: The oceanic plate sinks beneath the continental plate
cards.why: Oceanic crust is denser than continental crust. It sinks into the mantle, forming a trench and a volcanic arc.
cards.trap: Assuming the continental plate sinks because it is thicker; density, not thickness, controls subduction.

cards.q: A volcano has steep sides and alternating layers of lava and ash. Which type is it?
cards.why: Composite volcanoes form from viscous, silica-rich magma that traps gas. Alternating lava and ash layers build steep cones.
cards.trap: Confusing composite cones with shield volcanoes, which form from runny, low-silica lava.

cards.q: The point on Earth's surface directly above an earthquake's focus is called the...
cards.why: Seismic waves start at the focus underground. The point directly above it on the surface is the epicenter.
cards.trap: Using hypocenter for the surface point; the hypocenter is the underground focus.

cards.q: Which fault forms when the crust is stretched by tension?
cards.why: Normal faults form in tension. The hanging wall slides down the fault plane because the crust is being pulled apart.
cards.trap: Mixing up normal and reverse faults; reverse faults form under compression.

cards.q: Why do S-waves fail to pass through Earth's outer core?
choices: The outer core is extremely dense
cards.why: S-waves are shear waves. Liquids cannot support shear stress, so these waves cannot travel through the liquid outer core.
cards.trap: Thinking density alone blocks S-waves; it is the liquid state that removes shear strength.

cards.q: Which mineral is hardest on the Mohs hardness scale?
cards.why: Diamond ranks 10 on the Mohs scale, the top value. Talc ranks 1 and quartz ranks 7.
cards.trap: Choosing quartz because it scratches glass; diamond is much harder than quartz.

cards.q: Which pair of processes turns loose sediment into sedimentary rock?
cards.why: Buried sediment is squeezed by compaction. Minerals then precipitate and cement the grains together.
cards.trap: Believing heat and pressure alone make sedimentary rock; that path makes metamorphic rock.

cards.q: Which process is an example of chemical weathering?
cards.why: Oxygen reacts with iron minerals to form rust. This changes the mineral composition, so it is chemical weathering.
cards.trap: Treating frost wedging as chemical because water is involved; it is physical weathering.

cards.q: Which statement describes erosion rather than weathering?
choices: Sand is carried downstream by a river
Feldspar alters to clay in place
Ice expands inside a rock crack
Iron in rock reacts with oxygen
cards.answer: Sand is carried downstream by a river
cards.why: Erosion moves material from one place to another. Weathering only breaks rock down where it sits.
cards.trap: Calling any rock breakdown erosion; only transport counts as erosion.

cards.q: A limestone layer is baked by nearby magma and recrystallizes. Which rock forms?
cards.why: Heat from magma recrystallizes limestone without melting it. The product is marble; sandstone would become quartzite.
cards.trap: Choosing quartzite because both are non-foliated; quartzite forms from sandstone.

cards.q: In which atmospheric layer do most weather events occur?
cards.why: The troposphere holds most of the atmosphere's mass and nearly all its water vapor. Weather forms there.
cards.trap: Placing weather in the stratosphere because ozone absorbs sunlight there.

cards.q: Which cloud type is associated with thunderstorms and heavy rain?
cards.why: Cumulonimbus clouds have strong vertical growth. Their ice crystals and rapid updrafts produce thunder and heavy rain.
cards.trap: Linking heavy rain to stratus clouds because both look gray and flat.

cards.q: Which condition favors the formation of a tropical cyclone?
cards.why: Evaporation from warm water supplies the latent heat that powers a tropical cyclone. Cool water cannot sustain it.
cards.trap: Thinking strong wind shear helps; shear tilts and tears the storm apart.

cards.q: Which monsoon brings the rainy season to the Philippines?
cards.why: The southwest monsoon (habagat) flows from the warm ocean toward the country. It carries moist air and brings most of the wet-season rain. The northeast monsoon (amihan) is the cool, dry season.
cards.trap: Swapping habagat with amihan; amihan is the cool, dry northeast monsoon.

cards.q: Why does rising air cool as it moves upward?
choices: It loses heat to the ozone layer
It slows down and loses kinetic energy
cards.why: Air pressure falls with altitude. The rising parcel expands, does work, and cools adiabatically.
cards.trap: Saying heat is lost to space; the cooling comes from expansion, not radiation.

cards.q: Which gas is released by burning fossil fuels and absorbs outgoing infrared radiation?
cards.why: Fossil fuel combustion releases carbon dioxide. CO_2 absorbs outgoing infrared radiation and warms the lower atmosphere.
cards.trap: Choosing oxygen because it is abundant; O_2 has no dipole moment and does not absorb infrared.

cards.q: What happens to infrared radiation emitted by Earth's surface?
choices: It is absorbed by greenhouse gases
It is reflected back by the ozone layer
It becomes visible light in the troposphere
cards.answer: It is absorbed by greenhouse gases
cards.why: Greenhouse gases absorb outgoing infrared radiation. They re-emit it in all directions, including back toward the surface.
cards.trap: Thinking the atmosphere reflects infrared; greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit it.

cards.q: Which process changes water vapor into liquid droplets?
cards.why: Cooling air cannot hold as much water vapor. Excess vapor condenses onto particles and forms droplets.
cards.trap: Confusing condensation with evaporation since both change the state of water.

cards.q: What mainly drives surface ocean currents?
cards.why: Winds drag on the sea surface and transfer momentum. This wind stress sets surface currents in motion.
cards.trap: Assuming tides drive surface currents; tides are minor compared with wind stress.

cards.q: Which layer of Earth is liquid and produces the magnetic field?
cards.why: The outer core is liquid iron and nickel. Its convection, coupled with Earth's rotation, generates the magnetic field.
cards.trap: Choosing the inner core because it is hottest; the inner core is solid.

cards.q: Which principle says that in undisturbed sedimentary layers, the lowest layer is the oldest?
cards.why: In an undisturbed sequence, each layer was deposited on top of the older layer below it.
cards.trap: Confusing superposition with original horizontality, which is about flat deposition.

cards.q: Which planet is the largest in the solar system?
cards.why: Jupiter is the most massive planet. Its mass is more than twice that of all the other planets combined.
cards.trap: Choosing Saturn because of its rings; Jupiter is larger.

cards.q: Which of these is a terrestrial planet?
cards.why: Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars have rocky surfaces. Mars is the only terrestrial planet listed.
cards.trap: Picking Jupiter or Saturn because they are planets; both are gas giants.

cards.q: According to Kepler's second law, a planet moves fastest when it is...
choices: at the midpoint of its orbit
cards.why: Equal areas are swept in equal times. The planet covers the same area faster when it is near the Sun.
cards.trap: Thinking a planet moves fastest at aphelion because its orbit path is longer there.

cards.q: Where is the main asteroid belt located?
cards.why: The main belt lies in the gap between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
cards.trap: Placing the belt between Earth and Mars; the main belt lies beyond Mars.

cards.q: Kepler's third law states that the square of a planet's orbital period is proportional to...
choices: the cube of its semi-major axis
the square of its semi-major axis
the inverse of its semi-major axis
cards.answer: the cube of its semi-major axis
cards.why: For the solar system, T^2 = a^3 with T in years and a in AU. So T^2 is proportional to a^3.
cards.trap: Using T proportional to a, which drops both the square and the cube.

cards.q: If the distance between two masses is doubled, the gravitational force between them becomes...
cards.why: Newton's law gives F proportional to 1/r^2. Doubling r makes F one-fourth of its original value.
cards.trap: Doubling the force when the distance doubles, which reverses the inverse-square relation.

cards.q: Which Moon phase occurs when the Moon is between Earth and the Sun?
cards.why: The Moon sits between Earth and the Sun. Its sunlit side faces away from Earth, so we see no illuminated face.
cards.trap: Confusing new moon with full moon; at full moon Earth is between the Sun and the Moon.

cards.q: A lunar eclipse can occur only during which phase?
cards.why: Earth must lie between the Sun and the Moon. That alignment happens only at full moon.
cards.trap: Choosing new moon because the Moon looks dark; lunar eclipses need the full moon.

cards.q: Why is there not a solar eclipse at every new moon?
choices: The Moon's orbit is tilted about 5 degrees to Earth's orbital plane
The Moon is too small to cover the Sun
cards.answer: The Moon's orbit is tilted about 5 degrees to Earth's orbital plane
cards.why: The Moon's orbit is tilted about 5 degrees from the ecliptic. Most new moons pass above or below the Sun.
cards.trap: Assuming eclipses need only alignment; the orbital tilt usually breaks the alignment.

cards.q: Which tide occurs when the Sun, Earth, and Moon are aligned?
cards.why: At new and full moon the solar and lunar tidal bulges add up, giving the largest tidal range.
cards.trap: Linking spring tide to the spring season; the name refers to the water springing up.

cards.q: About how long is one complete cycle of lunar phases?
cards.why: The synodic month averages about 29.5 days. The sidereal month of 27.3 days is shorter because Earth also moves.
cards.trap: Using the 27.3-day sidereal month for the phase cycle.

cards.q: What surface property mainly determines a star's color?
cards.why: Hot stars radiate most strongly at short wavelengths and look blue. Cool stars look red.
cards.trap: Reading color as distance; distance affects brightness, not color.

cards.q: Where on the H-R diagram do most stars, including the Sun, lie?
cards.why: Stars fuse hydrogen into helium on the main sequence. This stable stage is the longest part of a star's life.
cards.trap: Placing the Sun with the red giants because it looks yellow; it is a main-sequence star.

cards.q: What remains at the center of a planetary nebula left by a Sun-like star?
cards.why: A Sun-like star sheds its outer layers as a planetary nebula. The exposed core remains as a white dwarf.
cards.trap: Choosing a neutron star; only massive stars leave neutron stars.

cards.q: Why do different constellations appear in the night sky each season?
choices: Earth orbits the Sun and faces a different part of space
The stars move quickly around Earth each year
Earth's axis tilt changes every year
The Moon blocks different stars each season
cards.answer: Earth orbits the Sun and faces a different part of space
cards.why: Earth's night side faces a different direction as it orbits the Sun. Different constellations become visible.
cards.trap: Thinking the stars themselves move fast; Earth's orbit changes our view.

cards.q: A light-year is a unit of...
cards.why: A light-year is the distance light travels in one year, about 9.5 x 10^12 km.
cards.trap: Reading light-year as a time; it measures distance despite the word year.

cards.q: Which observation is the strongest evidence that the universe is expanding?
cards.why: Light from receding galaxies is stretched to longer wavelengths. Greater redshift with distance indicates expansion.
cards.trap: Thinking expansion means galaxies only move through space; space itself stretches.

cards.q: What type of galaxy is the Milky Way?
cards.why: The Milky Way has a central bar and spiral arms. Radio and infrared maps confirm this structure.
cards.trap: Choosing elliptical because of the bright central bulge; the disk and bar make it a spiral.
